text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary latency SLO breach for runtime-service (us-west-2). p95 ~= 430ms (SLO 200ms). Alert: https://grafana.internal/g/runtime/alrt/12345 :rotating_light:

sahil: oncall here, ACKing. which rollout id is this? paging devs who pushed canary.

morgan: that was the canary from release deploy-20260315-72a — pushed kernel selection change + batching tweak. Canary at 30% traffic in us-west only.

janet: looking at graphs — latency spike coincides with canary start. interestingly GPU utilization dropped on canary pods while CPU spikes + long tail in nvtx timings. seems like kernel fallback happened and batch assembly stalled. prefix KV cache hit rate fell from 0.87 -> 0.12 at the same time. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/runtime-canary

kevin: I'm on infra. if kernel fallback is tripping, can we flip the runtime feature flag to force previous kernel set? which flag name?

morgan: flag is ff/runtime/kernel_fallback_enabled (default true). For rollback behavior we can flip ff/runtime/use_legacy_kernels=true OR kill batching path with ff/runtime/prefer_batching=false to isolate. I'd prefer killing fallback first: set ff/runtime/kernel_fallback_enabled=false for canary group.

sahil: do NOT make global changes yet — limit to canary group. I'll pause the canary rollout now.

release-bot: rollout deploy-20260315-72a paused (scope: canary us-west-2, user: sahil).

sahil: executing targeted flag override for canary pods (us-west-2) in LaunchDarkly.

morgan: while that's happening, can someone grab a heap of traces for a slow request? use service.traceId header or client id 0x3f4a.

janet: retrieving traces... also running quick query on prefix/cache hits:
```
# prometheus
sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_hit[5m])) / sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_requests[5m]))
```
Result dropped to ~0.12 at 14:07 PDT when canary began.

kevin: flag flip applied to canary group (confirmed). monitoring for 60s.

morgan: still seeing p95 ~420ms. kernel fallback flag didn't snap us back — suggests the code path might have modified batching handshake or KV lookup keys. Might need rollback.

sahil: agreed. canary stability is not returning. I'm initiating targeted rollback of canary pods to previous replicaSet.

kevin: running:
```
kubectl --context=prod-us-west rollout undo deployment/runtime-service --to-revision=42 -n prod --selector=canary=true
```

release-bot: rollback started for runtime-service (canary us-west-2) by sahil.

janet: metrics are improving as new pods come up — p95 trending down to 210ms after rollback starts. KV cache hit warms back to ~0.8.

morgan: inspecting the canary image — commit 72a introduced a change in kv cache key hashing (short-circuit for 0-length prefix) + changed the batching window from 20ms -> 50ms when a kernel fallback occurs. The combination increases small-request latency and prevents good batching.

sahil: root cause hypothesis: commit 72a's kernel fallback path increases batching latency (50ms) and causes cache key inconsistency leading to cache churn.

dmitri: opening an incident ticket: INC-20260315-7. will add owner tags and a follow-up action item to revert the kernel-fallback change and add unit tests for cache key stability.

sahil: customer impact assessment: Hosted API customers routed to us-west-2 saw ~20% requests experience >2x latency for small-response endpoints for the 15 minutes when canary was at 30%. No token corruption or data loss observed. Impacted customers list gathered from request routing logs; approx 12 tenants affected. Recommend proactive credits for affected usage window.

morgan: creating PR to revert commit 72a and add a short-term guard to avoid increasing batching window when fallback engages. PR: https://git.internal/r/runtime/PR/2481

kevin: post-rollback verification — running synthetic traffic against runtime-service in us-west:
```
hey -z 5s -c 50 -m POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
p95 now ~180ms.

incident-bot: CUSTOMER IMPACT: partial latency degradation in us-west-2 for ~15m window. Severity: SEV3 -> recommend postmortem.

sahil: I'm going to hand off to dmitri for overnight monitoring and follow-up with the release owner. Things to include in handoff: traces saved in /s3/internal/incidents/INC-20260315-7/traces.tar.gz, profile samples, kube events, and the rollback steps taken.

dmitri: taking handoff. I'll keep watch on the canary hold and the revert PR. Adding follow-ups: (1) revert + harden (2) add e2e that exercises kv cache keys across batching boundaries (3) add alert for cache hit rate drop to fire sooner.

sahil: notes for postmortem: timeline, root cause hypothesis (kernel fallback + batching window), mitigation (paused canary, flag override, targeted rollback), customer impact, action items. I'll draft initial timeline and share here tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:

morgan: big thanks for fast response. we should also add a deploy-gate to block kernel fallback changes without perf gating.

dmitri: acknowledged. I'll include that as an action. Handing off to oncall dmitri at 23:20 PDT.

sahil: closing on-call for this immediate incident. If p95 climbs >300ms for >5m escalate to SEV2.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED (status: mitigated, incident: INC-20260315-7)
